reason: This is the only offered combination, and the calcium signal may allow the filaments to interact.

effect: Calcium exposes the grip sites, allowing myosin to pull the filaments past one another. The remaining step appears to address relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments sliding is clear and useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and pumping calcium back into storage seems necessary for the fibre to relax.
expectation: I expect the calcium pumps to reduce calcium around the filaments so the fibre can relax and become ready to pull again.

effect: The result completes the pull-and-relax cycle: ATP powers calcium's return to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping pulling.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work, and the outside pull explains how the fibre lengthens again.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium signal producing a shortening fibre was the strongest moment. It connected the signal to myosin's repeated pulls and made clear that the filaments slide rather than shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Packing the filament units into the fibre was clear but predictable; its result added little explanation beyond the assembly itself.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin release and reset, and it also powers calcium's return to storage during relaxation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though several were the only offered combination, so choosing them involved little decision-making.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how this working fibre contributes to a larger body system. The sequence made the cellular mechanism clear, although the later choices became predictable.
